text.arabic_uthmani: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُنَزِّلُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقًۭا ۚ وَمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ إِلَّا مَن يُنِيبُ

words.gloss_range: independent resumptive pronoun that makes the known divine referent the visible subject before the action predicates begin
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) starts by making the divine referent explicit before any act is named. That visible subject header keeps the owner of judgment from 40:12 active, then lets the following relative frame define the same one through showing signs and sending provision. Because the pronoun stands outside the later verbs, the two actions read as one identity profile rather than as loose events.

topics.headline: resumed divine subject made visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader carries the divine owner of judgment from 40:12 into this ayah as the same actor who now shows and provides.
topics.reason: The cross-reference support resolves the pronoun to the prior divine referent, and the nominal opening makes that referent the subject anchor for the relative predicate.

topics.headline: subject header before the action chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actor is foregrounded first, so the later verbs are processed as predicates of one visible subject.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun is not required merely to carry verbal agreement; it creates a visible subject header before the relative clause begins.

topics.headline: identity block before response block
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah divide into divine identity through gifts and then a restricted human response.
topics.reason: The clause structure supports an opening identity frame before the later negated remembrance clause.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun binding the visible subject to the following two divine actions as one identifying description
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) binds the opening subject to a following description. Its masculine singular agreement keeps the profile centered on one actor, while its relative force gathers showing and sending into one descriptive span. The word therefore prevents the two positive imperfect verbs from drifting apart before the ayah turns to negated remembrance.

topics.headline: singular relative keeps one actor in view
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps one divine actor in view while multiple actions unfold.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun agrees with the singular subject and introduces the predicate expression attached to it.

topics.headline: two actions form one relative profile
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears showing signs and sending provision as one identity-description rather than two separate reports.
topics.reason: The relative clause spans the coordinated positive predicates and closes before the response clause.

topics.headline: relative span closes before response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can separate the completed divine-action profile from the later test of human uptake.
topics.reason: The fixed relative form binds the following clause to the subject, and the later conjunction opens a new response unit.

words.gloss_range: Form IV caused perception with the addressees as direct object; locally showing signs so that evidence presses toward recognition
words.root_gloss_range: sight, perception, vision, and judgment; the local Form IV selects induced perception while the broader field colors sight as evidentiary assessment
words.prose: {{ar:يُرِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:yurīkum}}) makes the addressees direct recipients of caused perception. The Form IV frame means the signs are made perceptible to them, not merely left visible in the world, and the act is one-directional disclosure rather than mutual appearance or self-display. The broader sight-and-judgment field makes that perception accountable: the ayah later asks whether being made to see becomes inward remembrance. In sequence, this first divine action gives evidence before provision, and the same addressed group then reappears as beneficiaries and as the audience of the next command (40:14). The exact pairing of showing verb and possessed signs also recurs at 40:81, so the local sign-remembrance test sits inside a repeated sign-display formula.

topics.headline: addressees are made to perceive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the audience as directly made to perceive evidence, so ignorance cannot be treated as simple non-exposure.
topics.reason: The Form IV verb takes the second-person suffix as object and the possessed signs as the thing shown.

topics.headline: seeing presses toward judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sight is not inert exposure; it presses toward recognition and later remembrance.
topics.reason: The broader root field supports sight joined to judgment, but the missing V4 root data and local Form IV frame keep the claim to interpretive pressure rather than an activated separate derivative.

topics.headline: one-directional disclosure, not mutual display
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine disclosure moving toward the audience rather than a reciprocal or self-advertising act.
topics.reason: The local form is causative Form IV and the valency frame is transitive with object suffix and explicit object.

topics.headline: evidence comes before provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that knowledge-gift comes first, before material provision and before the restrictive test of remembrance.
topics.reason: The verb opens the first predicate unit and its object is completed before the provision clause begins.

topics.headline: same audience receives evidence and obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same second-person group from prior exposure through present evidence and toward the command of 40:14.
topics.reason: The suffix on the verb, the beneficiary phrase, and the next-ayah command keep the addressee chain active across the boundary.

topics.headline: shown signs tested by remembrance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears caused perception tied to the sign object and tested by later remembrance, with the same sign-showing formula echoed at 40:81.
topics.reason: The local verb-object pairing and the explicit 40:81 comparison support an echo without making 40:81 govern the local parse.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural signs as the object made visible; locally evidentiary pointers owned by the same divine subject
words.root_gloss_range: sign, mark, proof, lesson, and verse-unit range; locally the caused-seeing frame selects evidentiary signs while allowing a broader proof-field
words.prose: {{ar:ءَايَٰتِهِۦ}} ({{tr:ʾāyātihi}}) names what is made visible: multiple signs possessed by the same singular subject. The plural broadens the proof-field, while the suffix gathers every sign back to one owner. The sign range can include visible marks and revealed units, but the local object slot after the showing verb selects evidentiary pointers, not free-floating wonders. That owned evidence helps bridge 40:12 and 40:14: the one whose judgment was named is the owner of the signs and the one to be invoked.

topics.headline: possessed signs complete the showing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the evidence as owned by the divine subject and as the concrete content of caused perception.
topics.reason: The noun is the direct object of the showing verb and carries a third-person possessive suffix tied to the same referent.

topics.headline: broad sign field narrowed to evidentiary pointers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof-field is larger than one medium while the local syntax keeps the signs functioning as evidence shown to the audience.
topics.reason: The lexical range is broad, but local caused-perception syntax selects the signs as evidentiary objects.

topics.headline: root-dispute pressure meets return theme
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a limited resonance between signs and return, because the ayah later defines the remembering person by turning back.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute may supply resonance with the final return verb, but it does not replace the local sign/proof sense.

topics.headline: many signs, one owner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears multiple evidentiary units gathered under one singular owner.
topics.reason: The plural construct form multiplies the signs while the singular possessive suffix keeps their source unified.

topics.headline: owned evidence grounds the next command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the owner of the signs toward the explicit invocation command in 40:14.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix and the next-ayah command create a referent-chain from judgment, to signs, to invocation.

topics.headline: first gift-object before provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a pair of gifts: possessed signs shown first and open-ended provision sent second.
topics.reason: The first object closes the showing segment before the descent clause supplies a second object.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the second positive present verb to the first inside the same relative profile
words.prose: The first {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the internal joint of the divine-action profile. It comes after the shown-sign object and before the descent verb, so it joins predicate frames rather than nouns. This keeps evidence and provision coordinated under the same relative description while preparing a contrast with the later conjunction that opens the negated response clause.

topics.headline: second positive verb joined to the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears showing and sending as coordinated actions of the same subject, not as appositional restatement.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence joins the descent verb to the showing verb within the relative predicate.

topics.headline: joint between completed predicate frames
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first gift is complete before the second predicate begins.
topics.reason: The conjunction occurs after the first verb-object unit and before the second verb.

topics.headline: first conjunction differs from the response pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the conjunction that adds a divine gift from the later conjunction that pivots into human non-remembrance.
topics.reason: The first conjunction joins positive predicates, while the later conjunction launches a new negated response unit.

words.gloss_range: transitive descent verb gathering beneficiary, elevated source, and provision object into one ongoing divine dispatch frame
words.root_gloss_range: descent, sending down, arrival, lodging, and staged bringing-down; locally provision is sent down in a transitive frame
words.prose: {{ar:يُنَزِّلُ}} ({{tr:yunazzilu}}) begins the second positive act under the same subject: provision is being sent down for the addressees, from an elevated source, as an explicit object. The descent image keeps the gift vertical and dispatched rather than abstract. The Form II reading highlights ordered, intensive sending down; the accepted Form IV variant can be noted as a causative contrast, but the local surface and grammar keep the transitive provision frame in place. This present-tense provision turns the judge-owner from 40:12 into the provider whose gifts ground the command of 40:14. The clause also joins the familiar descent-provision pattern seen in 2:22 while keeping this ayah's local beneficiary-source-object frame intact.

topics.headline: beneficiary, source, and object in one frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees provision as a structured divine dispatch with recipient, source, and object all in view.
topics.reason: The verb governs the beneficiary phrase, the source phrase, and the explicit provision object.

topics.headline: present dispatch of provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears provision as an ongoing present gift, not only a past proof or general doctrine.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb and surrounding present predicates support ongoing dispatch in the ayah's divine-action profile.

topics.headline: descent gives provision vertical arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels provision as sent down from above rather than as an abstract benefit appearing without route.
topics.reason: The root image and the source phrase support vertical descent and staged arrival while local grammar keeps provision as the object.

topics.headline: Form II staging with accepted variant contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the main surface stresses ordered sending down, while the variant contrast stays within the same descent-provision event.
topics.reason: The local surface is Form II, so variant Form IV evidence is useful contrast but does not replace the local form.

topics.headline: second action parallels showing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second divine action match the first while shifting the gift from perception to provision.
topics.reason: The coordinated imperfect verbs and the source-object phrase create a local echo between showing and sending.

topics.headline: judge-owner appears as provider
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same divine referent from judgment to provision to the obligation of invocation in 40:14.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the prior judgment setting, the present provider description, and the following command.

topics.headline: provision formula has wider parallels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this provision clause with the familiar descent-provision pattern in 2:22 without losing the local syntax.
topics.reason: The 2:22 comparison is concrete and formulaic, while the local frame remains governed by this verb and its complements.

words.gloss_range: benefactive prepositional phrase with second-person plural suffix, marking the addressees as recipients of provision without making them its source
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُم}} ({{tr:lakum}}) recasts the same addressed group as beneficiaries. The suffix repeats the audience already made to perceive signs, while the preposition marks provision as for them without making them its owner or source. That pronoun direction matters because the next ayah reverses the relation into devotion for Him (40:14).

topics.headline: same audience becomes beneficiary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same addressees from direct perceivers of signs to recipients of provision.
topics.reason: The second-person plural suffix repeats the audience of the showing verb and is governed by the beneficiary preposition.

topics.headline: recipient benefit without source ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the addressees as beneficiaries of provision, not possessors of the source from which it descends.
topics.reason: The beneficiary phrase attaches to the descent verb, while the source phrase remains distinct.

topics.headline: from provision for you to devotion for Him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that benefit directed to the audience becomes the ground for the audience's directed devotion in 40:14.
topics.reason: The benefactive suffix and the following command create a reciprocal movement from received gift to required invocation.

topics.headline: recipient slot completed by provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader waits for the object that names the benefit assigned to the addressees.
topics.reason: The beneficiary phrase is filled out by the later provision object in the same descent frame.

words.gloss_range: source preposition governing the elevated source phrase in the descent frame; partitive nuance is possible but secondary to source attachment here
words.prose: {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) opens the source phrase for the descent. It governs the following elevated noun as the source complement of the sending-down verb, so the phrase should not be flattened into a loose modifier of provision alone. Its range can allow source and partitive pressure, but local attachment makes origin the controlling relation.

topics.headline: source phrase governed by descent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears provision descending from a named source, not merely receiving an atmospheric descriptor.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the following noun as source complement of the descent verb.

topics.headline: partitive range under source attachment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader retains a sense of provision coming out from the elevated domain while local grammar keeps source attachment primary.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row allows qualification of provision, but the guardrail explicitly preserves the phrase as source complement of the verb rather than modifier alone.

topics.headline: source boundary marked in the form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition as the boundary where descent is routed from source toward gift.
topics.reason: The preposition is the formal marker introducing the governed source noun.

words.gloss_range: definite singular elevated source governed by the preceding source preposition inside the descent-provision clause
words.root_gloss_range: height, elevation, sky, and elevated domain; locally the definite noun names the source domain of provision, not an independent actor
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّمَآءِ}} ({{tr:al-samāʾi}}) is governed as the source domain of the descent. Its height field makes provision arrive from above, and its definite singular form names one elevated domain rather than a vague weather layer. The elevation language also answers the exalted-title setting of 40:12 by making abstract height concrete in the source phrase. Its extended vocal form suits that elevated source without changing the grammar. Other derivational disputes about marking are useful only as contrast; the local word selects elevation and source. The source-provision pattern can be compared with 51:22 and 2:22, but here the phrase remains the governed origin of the descent before the provision object is named.

topics.headline: sky as governed source, not actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the elevated noun as the source of descent, not as an independent actor.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the source preposition attached to the descent verb.

topics.headline: elevated domain, not mere weather
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the source as an elevated domain of divine provision rather than a mere meteorological layer.
topics.reason: The root image and concrete noun support elevated-domain sense in the local source phrase.

topics.headline: abstract elevation becomes source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the previous elevation language become concrete as the place from which provision descends.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the prior title setting to the source phrase in this ayah.

topics.headline: marking dispute remains contrastive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local word is governed by elevation, while marking-language alternatives do not control the sense here.
topics.reason: The dispute helps separate elevation from marking, but local grammar and the root field select the elevated-source sense.

topics.headline: origin named before object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader receives the origin of provision before the object itself is named.
topics.reason: The source phrase stands between the descent verb and the provision object.

topics.headline: source phrase echoes provision formulae
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this source-provision grammar with 51:22 and 2:22 while preserving the local source-complement role.
topics.reason: The cited parallels use concrete references for the source-provision pattern without overriding local syntax.

topics.headline: form lengthens the source word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a formal elongation that suits the elevated source word without changing its grammatical role.
topics.reason: The form-specific note is locally coherent but secondary to source-governance and elevation.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative provision object of the descent verb, naming an open-ended allotted benefit sent for the addressees
words.root_gloss_range: provision, allotted support, sustenance, and giver-relation; locally the object is what is sent down, while the addressees are beneficiaries
words.prose: {{ar:رِزْقًۭا}} ({{tr:rizqan}}) is the object sent down, not the source or the beneficiary. Its indefinite form keeps the provision open-ended, while the root field makes it allotted support from a giver rather than mere possession. The word completes the second gift in the relative profile: signs are shown, provision is sent, and that received benefit becomes part of the ground for invocation in 40:14. Its wider provider-field echoes, including 51:58 and 2:22, sharpen the giver-relation without changing the local accusative object role.

topics.headline: provision is the object sent down
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps provision as the gift sent down while the humans remain beneficiaries.
topics.reason: The noun is the explicit accusative object of the descent verb.

topics.headline: indefinite allotted support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears provision as an open category of allotted support rather than a single named commodity.
topics.reason: The indefinite noun and root field support broad allotted benefit within the local object slot.

topics.headline: giver-relation without seeking frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the provider relation behind the gift while the local clause keeps the addressees as recipients, not seekers producing provision.
topics.reason: Provider and seeking derivatives color the semantic economy, but local syntax names provision as the sent object.

topics.headline: maṣdar-like form broadens the category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears provision as a category of allotment-result rather than a tightly delimited item.
topics.reason: The local form is tagged as gerund-like and indefinite, supporting category breadth.

topics.headline: received provision grounds invocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees material gift join shown signs as a reason the addressees are commanded to call in 40:14.
topics.reason: The provision object completes the gift pair and participates in the move to the next command.

topics.headline: provider field echoes concrete parallels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the provider economy behind the local gift through 51:58 and 2:22 without replacing the local object role.
topics.reason: The cited parallels are concrete provider/provision references and remain supportive rather than controlling.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new response unit after the completed pair of divine gifts
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is not another internal joint inside the gift sequence. It comes after provision has been named and immediately before negation, so it opens a new response unit. The effect is sharp: after evidence and provision, the ayah pivots to the surprising failure of remembrance.

topics.headline: conjunction pivots to response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah turn from what God gives to what humans fail to take in.
topics.reason: The conjunction launches the negated response clause rather than simply adding a third divine action.

topics.headline: gift sequence closed before negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that non-remembrance is evaluated only after the two gifts have been completed.
topics.reason: The word stands after the provision object and before the negative particle.

topics.headline: addition carries contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sequel to generosity as contrastive: gifts are given, yet remembrance is restricted.
topics.reason: The conjunction binds the negated clause to the prior gifts while shifting its discourse function.

words.gloss_range: negative particle beginning the left side of the restrictive frame completed by the later exception particle
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) begins the denial that the later exception will narrow. It is a negative particle here, not a relative pronoun, and it puts the remembering predicate under broad negation before any positive subject appears. After signs and provision, this blocks the easy equation that exposure plus benefit automatically produces heed.

topics.headline: negation begins the only-structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first feels remembrance broadly denied before the exception admits one class.
topics.reason: The particle begins the negation-exception construction whose scope is explicitly supported by attachment evidence.

topics.headline: negative particle, not relative pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not mistake the word for a relative marker; it denies remembrance without narrowing the denial by person or number.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as a negative particle, and the paired exception supplies the restriction.

topics.headline: gifts do not automatically yield heed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the gap between receiving evidence and provision and actually becoming heedful.
topics.reason: The negation follows the completed gift pair and precedes the remembering verb, making the response failure explicit.

words.gloss_range: Form V imperfect remembering or heed-taking, intransitive here under negation and exception; object omission generalizes the response
words.root_gloss_range: remembering, mention, reminder, and reminding; locally the Form V verb selects inward appropriation of reminder rather than a named reminder-agent or mutual discussion
words.prose: {{ar:يَتَذَكَّرُ}} ({{tr:yatadhakkaru}}) is the response predicate placed under negation until the exception arrives. With no overt object, it means becoming heedful generally, not recalling one item from the previous clause. Its Form V shape makes reminder inwardly received and appropriated, while excluding a mutual-discussion frame. The memory-and-mention field lets true heed reorder inward awareness and outward mention, but the local verb remains receptive remembrance. The verb therefore gathers the shown signs and descended provision into a test: do gifts become remembered meaning that can lead to the invocation commanded in 40:14? The restriction also sharpens the comparison with 39:9, where remembrance is likewise limited to a qualified class.

topics.headline: objectless remembering becomes general heed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a general heed-taking capacity, not recall of one named object.
topics.reason: The verb appears without an overt object and is tagged intransitive in the local frame.

topics.headline: ongoing heed placed under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees remembrance as the human predicate tested after the divine actions, not as a third positive divine act.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb is the predicate inside the negation-exception response clause.

topics.headline: memory and mention field narrowed to heed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses that true heed can reorder both inward awareness and outward mention, while the local verb remains receptive remembrance.
topics.reason: The broader root field is relevant, but local Form V and intransitive frame select inward heed-taking.

topics.headline: reminder must be appropriated inwardly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that external showing is not enough; the reminder must be taken into the self.
topics.reason: The Form V pattern supports receptive or reflexive force and foregrounds uptake rather than a named reminder-agent.

topics.headline: not a mutual recollection mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not relocate the response into group discussion; the ayah tests inward heed-taking.
topics.reason: The selected form is Form V, not a mutual-discussion form.

topics.headline: heed links evidence to invocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees inward heed as the bridge between evidence received and invocation commanded in 40:14.
topics.reason: Inter-ayah rows connect the response failure of 40:12, the gifts of 40:13, and the command of 40:14.

topics.headline: signs and provision become interpretive uptake
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears remembrance as the interpretive uptake of the ayah's gifts, comparable to the restricted remembering of 39:9.
topics.reason: The verb follows both gifts and has a concrete inter-ayah comparison that restricts remembrance to a qualified class.

words.gloss_range: exception particle completing the negation-exception restriction and admitting only the following returning subject class
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) turns the prior negation into an only-structure. Because it stands after the remembering verb and before the returning-person phrase, the restriction applies to successful heed, not to the universality of the signs or provision. It delays the positive subject until the end, making the return verb the ayah's final interpretive key and part of the ground for the command in 40:14.

topics.headline: exception turns denial into exclusivity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the negative clause become an exclusive statement about who can remember.
topics.reason: The exception particle closes the scope opened by the negative particle and admits one class.

topics.headline: following phrase supplies the admitted subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the exception restrict the rememberer, not the divine gifts.
topics.reason: The particle occurs between the negated remembering verb and the following subject phrase.

topics.headline: positive subject delayed to the final key
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the return verb arrive as the final condition that grounds the following command in 40:14.
topics.reason: The exception delays the admitted subject until the final phrase, and the next ayah converts the diagnosis into command.

words.gloss_range: open animate relative or indefinite pronoun supplying the excepted subject class and controlling the following singular verbs distributively
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) supplies the only admitted remembering subject. It is personal and open: not a named individual or inherited group, but whoever fits the following return-action. Its singular agreement makes that open class distributive, one accountable returning subject at a time.

topics.headline: whoever fills the admitted subject slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees exactly who can perform the restricted act of remembering: the one defined by the following return.
topics.reason: The pronoun is the subject admitted by the exception and governs the following relative verb.

topics.headline: open personal class defined by return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the remembering class as accountable and behavioral, not genealogical or fixed.
topics.reason: The pronoun is animate and open in reference, and the following verb supplies the qualifying behavior.

topics.headline: singular agreement makes the class distributive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the open class is treated one person at a time through singular agreement.
topics.reason: The pronoun controls singular remembering and returning verbs while remaining open in reference.

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperfect return or turning-back verb qualifying the only remembering subject; objectless locally but context supplies orientation toward the divine actor
words.root_gloss_range: return, recurrence, taking turns, and reorientation; locally Form IV selects decisive turning back, with ongoing return-cycle pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يُنِيبُ}} ({{tr:yunību}}) gives the final qualification for the one who remembers. It is objectless, yet the context supplies direction toward the one who shows signs and sends provision. Its imperfect form and return-cycle root pressure make the person a continuing returner, not someone marked by a momentary reaction. Form IV makes the return a decisive reorientation that cannot be outsourced to a representative. After the prior rejection-belief contrast, this return names the corrective posture rather than mere exposure to signs. This closing posture anticipates the exclusive dedication commanded in 40:14 and aligns with the guidance-return pattern in 42:13 and the returning path of 31:15.

topics.headline: objectless return directed by context
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears return as absolute in wording but oriented by context toward the divine actor who gives signs and provision.
topics.reason: The verb lacks an explicit complement, and the preceding divine-action frame supplies the destination by context.

topics.headline: singular imperfect defines an ongoing returner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the open class defined distributively by ongoing return, not by a static label.
topics.reason: The verb agrees singularly with the open pronoun and appears in the imperfect.

topics.headline: return-cycle image becomes a profile
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses return as a continuing orientation and recognizable profile, while local grammar keeps the sense to turning back rather than generic rotation.
topics.reason: The broader root field supplies recurrence pressure, but the Form IV verb in context selects religious return.

topics.headline: direct reorientation, not outsourced relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the subject must turn back directly; the relation cannot be delegated.
topics.reason: The local Form IV verb supports decisive reorientation and excludes a representation-seeking pattern.

topics.headline: return anticipates exclusive invocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final return posture become the inner ground for exclusive invocation in 40:14.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the diagnostic close of 40:13 to the prescriptive command and dedication language of 40:14.

topics.headline: return corrects failed response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears return as the corrective posture after the prior rejection-belief contrast.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah row ties return to the response failures exposed before the current gifts.

topics.headline: return condition has concrete parallels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this return condition with guidance in 42:13 and the returning path in 31:15.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah references are concrete parallels for return as a condition of guidance and heed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated clauses يُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ and يُنَزِّلُ لَكُم ... رِزْقًا address the same plural recipients, while وَمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ إِلَّا مَن يُنِيبُ narrows successful uptake.
baseline_models.mechanism: Causative showing makes marks publicly available and downward delivery makes benefit materially available, but neither availability guarantees recognition. The exception clause relocates the decisive difference into the recipient: return converts exposed sign and received gift into active remembrance.

activation_trace.role: إراءة وإظهار supplies the causative act of making something available to another's sight.
The visible mark supplies inspectable content rather than a bare assertion.
إنزال الشيء وإيصاله supplies directed delivery from the giver to the addressed recipients.
The apportioned gift makes the descended object a benefit assigned to recipients.
Re-presencing after forgetting supplies the inward conversion of available evidence into recognition.
Habitual return supplies the directional response that completes the disclosure-gift circuit.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists signs and provision, then adds that a repentant person remembers.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages universally addressed disclosure and supply but selectively completed uptake: exposed marks and delivered benefit become remembrance only through recurrent reorientation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired forms يَتَذَكَّرُ and يُنِيبُ bind recovery of what has slipped from presence to repeated directional return.
baseline_models.mechanism: Remembering is not acquisition of wholly new information: the signs have already been shown and provision has already arrived. The remembrance branch restores an absent object to presence, while both return inventories supply recurrence; inabah is therefore the repeated operation by which disclosed reality is brought back into governing awareness.

activation_trace.role: استحضار الشيء بعد النسيان supplies recovery into present awareness.
The reminder image makes shown signs and received provision possible prompts for renewed presence.
رجوع الشيء مرة بعد أخرى supplies recurrence rather than a one-time turn.
Repeated return to a place or direction sharpens inabah as sustained reorientation toward a fixed source.

changed_reading.before: Only a person already disposed to repentance takes heed.
changed_reading.after: Taking heed is itself recursive: the returner repeatedly restores already-given signs and gifts to effective presence before they fade into familiarity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens with the Book's tanzil, whose branches combine composed writing with placement into a fitting station. When the focus later coordinates shown signs with descending provision, verbal revelation and material sustenance become two ordered deliveries: each arrives in a form and location through which its source can be read.

activation_trace.role: Putting a thing in its proper station lets the focus descent be tested as ordered placement, not mere downward motion.
The visible mark supplies the readable side of the focus delivery.
The opening tanzil activates ordering and fitting placement as the surah's first mode of descent.
Composed letters and the written object supply an organized, legible product of descent.

structural_cues: 40:2 establishes ن ز ل with the Book before 40:13 repeats the root for provision.
In 40:13 the same subject coordinates showing signs and sending provision to the same audience.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the lexical echo, composed writing, and fitting placement; I infer that the two descents share an ordering-and-delivery mechanism. A live alternative is that the echo marks only a common divine source while keeping revelation and provision functionally separate.

changed_reading.before: The Book descends verbally near the opening, while material provision descends independently in the focus.
changed_reading.after: The focus belongs to a surah-wide economy of ordered descent in which readable message and situated sustenance are coordinated forms of delivery.

context_deltas.mechanism: The return in يُنِيبُ is framed by an accepter at the surah's opening, a destination toward Him, a declared common return, and an explicit call-answer exchange. Inabah thus becomes relational motion: the recipient repeatedly answers a summons toward one who receives the turn, rather than merely correcting an interior state.

activation_trace.role: Habitual return supplies the repeated movement whose relational endpoints context discloses.
Acceptance with satisfaction supplies a receiving side for the act of return.
Becoming toward an outcome supplies the fixed destination named before the focus.
Return to a prior place supplies the declared common terminus of all competing calls.
Calling by speech supplies the summons to which reorientation can respond.
Answering speech supplies reciprocity rather than a one-way human movement.

structural_cues: 40:3 places acceptance of tawb and the destination toward Him before the focus's يُنِيبُ.
40:43 and 40:60 later align return, call, and answer while rejecting rival calls.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acceptance, destination, return, summons, and answer; I connect them into a reciprocal orientation circuit centered on يُنِيبُ. The live alternative is to keep inabah as unilateral devotion and treat call-answer as a separate prayer scene.

changed_reading.before: Inabah is an individual's inward repentance that permits remembrance.
changed_reading.after: Inabah is repeatedly answering a received call and moving toward an accepting destination; remembrance occurs inside that reciprocal relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Visible marks do not mechanically yield recognition. The earlier response path twists them into interlocking dispute, covers them, mistakes unstable gleam for substance, and repeatedly turns things off their face; later sealing fixes that response. The focus exception therefore names a counter-turn: inabah repeatedly restores orientation where argumentative processing repeatedly reverses it.

activation_trace.role: The visible mark is the common input that can be processed in opposed ways.
Repeated return supplies the restorative response path.
Interlocking contention supplies a processing mode that knots evidence into adversarial exchange.
Covering supplies active occlusion despite the sign's availability.
A gleam that does not hold supplies the deceptive surface by which movement through the lands misleads.
Turning a thing off its face supplies the directional inversion opposed to inabah.
Imprinting and sealing supplies the later fixation of repeated argumentative reversal.

structural_cues: 40:4 and 40:13 both place response to signs inside a negation-plus-exception construction: none disputes except one class, and none remembers except another.
The phrase disputing about God's signs recurs at 40:35 and 40:56, turning the early contrast into a surah-wide response pattern.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the mirrored exceptions and images of knotting, covering, deceptive sheen, reversal, and sealing; I infer two competing evidence-processing loops. A live alternative is that تَقَلُّب refers only to prosperous travel and contributes warning, not cognitive reversal.

changed_reading.before: Shown signs simply fail to persuade people who do not repent.
changed_reading.after: The same visible input bifurcates: one loop covers and reverses it through dispute, while recurrent return reorients it into remembrance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah explicitly builds an earned accounting channel and then separates provision from it. Deeds are recompensed, earnings are counted, and an evil is answered only by its like; yet the admitted are provisioned without account. The focus's apportioned rizq is therefore assigned gift, not wage: measured source and fitting distribution need not mean merit-equivalent payment.

activation_trace.role: The apportioned gift supplies allocation while leaving its relation to desert open.
Reciprocal recompense establishes the moral return channel.
Acquired gain supplies the deed-side input to reckoning.
Counting and calculation make the recompense channel explicitly accountable.
Like-for-like response limits the negative recompense described immediately before provision.
The repeated provision root transfers the focus's gift category into the explicit no-account contrast.
Negated counting marks provision as exceeding the ledger that governs recompense.

structural_cues: 40:17 joins recompense, earning, and swift account.
40:40 first limits recompense to equivalence and then repeats ر ز ق with بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated accounting vocabulary and an explicit no-account provision; I infer two distinct distributive channels and read focus rizq through the gift channel. 'Without account' may alternatively emphasize immeasurable abundance rather than absence of merit, but either reading blocks a simple wage equation.

changed_reading.before: The descended rizq is an apportioned allotment that could sound like measured compensation.
changed_reading.after: The descended rizq is assigned generosity rather than moral wages; the surah counts recompense but lets provision overflow calculation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Divine showing is enacted through directed fieldwork: move across the earth, focus sight or insight, and read surviving marks as evidence of an earlier process and its outcome. Tadhakkur becomes reconstructive trace-reading, not passive exposure; the returner lets remains of the past correct present orientation.

activation_trace.role: Sight and insight supply the focus capacity later exercised through travel and looking.
The visible mark supplies the evidential object instantiated by historical remains.
Restoring the absent supplies the temporal work of inferring former causes from present traces.
Movement and passage make showing an itinerary rather than a stationary spectacle.
Directed sight or insight supplies deliberate examination.
A remaining mark that indicates what was supplies the historical evidence mechanism.
The repeated command-frame renews movement as an evidential practice near the surah's close.
Repeated directed looking confirms that physical exposure still requires interpretive attention.
Repeated remains close the surah with the same trace-to-outcome inference.

structural_cues: 40:21 and 40:82 nearly repeat the travel-look-outcome-stronger-traces sequence.
The second sequence follows 40:81's exact renewal of وَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies travel, deliberate looking, surviving effects, and repeated outcome frames; I infer that these آثار instantiate one mode of the focus's signs. A live alternative keeps آثار as supporting historical proof while reserving آيات in 40:13 primarily for revelation and natural phenomena.

changed_reading.before: God places signs before an observer who may or may not notice them.
changed_reading.after: God's showing also recruits the observer into moving, comparing, and reconstructing causes from remains; remembrance is disciplined historical perception.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later recapitulation expands sky-provision into an inhabitable system: stable ground, sky as construction, formed bodies, and good provisions. The following staged bodily sequence runs from material origin through development to reasoning. Provision is thus not only an object falling from outside; it is the environmental and embodied support that makes a perceiving, remembering subject possible.

activation_trace.role: What is above and shelters supplies the environmental upper boundary of the focus descent.
Assigned benefit supplies the category later embedded in habitat and body.
Stability and settlement make the earth a support on which recipients can persist.
Building by joining parts makes the sky an organized shelter rather than only a source point.
Formed bodily image supplies the recipient-side architecture of provision.
The repeated provision root explicitly binds the recapitulated habitat to the focus gift.
Measured formation supplies the ordered developmental process of the recipient.
A continuum from drop to body supplies an inspectable material history within the recipient.
The restraint from ignorance supplies the cognitive endpoint named after the developmental sequence.

structural_cues: 40:64 repeats the focus's هُوَ/ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى, لَكُم, sky, and provision pattern while adding stable earth, built sky, and formed bodies.
40:67 follows with a material life-stage sequence ending in لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies environmental stability, construction, bodily form, provision, development, and cognition; I infer a coupled support system in which these conditions enable perception and remembrance. A live alternative treats 40:64 and 40:67 as adjacent but independent proofs rather than one causal system.

changed_reading.before: Provision is chiefly a descended commodity, plausibly rain or food, shown alongside signs.
changed_reading.after: Provision includes the stable habitat and formed, developing body that make seeing and reasoning possible; the recipient inhabits the sign before reflecting on it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus remembrance cannot mean mere eventual recall. Opponents are promised that they will remember the believer's words later, while he entrusts his affair now; only some promised outcome may be shown before universal return, and a sign is not demand-produced but permissioned. At the end, sight of overwhelming force yields faith that no longer benefits. Inabah therefore marks timely, actionable remembrance under partial noncoercive evidence, before forced seeing closes the response window.

structural_cues: 40:44 contrasts the believer's present entrusting with opponents' future remembering.

40:81-85 moves from renewed showing to historical inspection and finally to useless faith upon direct sight of force.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delayed recall, present entrusting, partial and permissioned showing, universal return, and useless faith after coercive sight; I infer a temporal response window and assign inabah the role of acting within it. A live alternative is that late faith fails because punishment is its object, not because partial evidence defines a general window.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's form-distant ر ء ي→ر و ي and س م و→و س م mappings, making showing bodily quenching and sky a marking rain. It remains valid as an exploratory mechanism because those split inventories are packet-supplied and converge with the focus branches that call rain provision and an ayah a visible mark. Downstream prose should present it as a cross-branch activation, not as a claim that the focus words etymologically mean irrigation or marking.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads Pharaoh's tower as a counter-machine to the focus's grammatical direction. It remains anchored in the focus's causative showing, downward sending, and sky source, while 40:36-37 explicitly joins building upward, reaching sky-connections, attempted inspection, beautification, and blockage. Downstream prose should qualify it as a spatial and political analogy, not as an assertion that every ascent is condemned or that the passages state this contrast explicitly.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates ن ز ل as prepared guest-fare inside the verb of descent and combines it with the later contrast between temporary useful goods and a permanent abode. It remains anchored in يُنَزِّلُ لَكُم رِزْقًا and recurrent return, with 40:39 supplying travel-use and settlement branches. Downstream prose should render it as a hospitality or waystation metaphor, not as the lexical replacement of 'sends down' with 'hosts.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يُنَزِّلُ لَكُم ... رِزْقًا and يُنِيبُ permit a host-gift-return configuration.

activation_trace.role: Prepared fare for a guest supplies hospitality as a latent image inside descended provision.
Assigned benefit supplies what the host makes available during the stay.
Habitual return supplies the guest's recurrent homeward orientation.

changed_reading.before: Provision is a commodity delivered for present use.
changed_reading.after: Provision can be carried as a host's prepared fare for a temporary stay; the one who returns receives it without mistaking the waystation for the settled home.

strongest_changes: The mirrored exception constructions make dispute-and-covering and return-and-remembrance rival processing loops for the same signs.
The surah distinguishes earned recompense from provision without account, preventing focus rizq from collapsing into wages.
Late recall and coerced sight can occur without benefit, so the focus privileges timely remembrance under partial evidence rather than mere eventual cognition.
Repeated travel-look-trace sequences turn divine showing into active historical reconstruction.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly re-ran the focus's core verbs in altered conditions: Book and provision descend, signs are disputed or traced, return becomes call-and-answer, and sight shifts from invitational to coercive. The split focus inventories also exposed a compact material reading in which rain both quenches and marks the earth.
remaining_uncertainties: The rain-as-inscription reading depends on form-distant split mappings and should remain exploratory rather than etymological.
The downward-disclosure/upward-capture contrast is a reader-supplied spatial arrow, though every element of the contrast is packet-anchored.
Provision 'without account' may foreground immeasurable abundance rather than a strict non-merit category, even though it still exceeds simple recompense.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Remembering depends on recurrent return.** `ذ ك ر/B003` supplies bringing a thing to mind, while `ن و ب/B001` supplies habitual return and recurring turns. The exclusive construction ties recollection to the returning subject. I infer that signs become legible through repeated reorientation; remembering reads as a cultivated return-path rather than passive storage.
2. **Provision is a landed sign.** `ن ز ل/B001` gives descent and settling, and `ر ز ق/B001` gives an allotted gift. Their proximity to “shows you His signs” lets material descent serve as demonstration. I infer that repeated provision makes the unseen giver perceptible; the ayah reads sustenance as epistemic as well as material.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The ordinary provisions and conveyances in 40:61 and 40:79–81 broaden descending provision into a network of repeatedly visible signs requiring recurrent return.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Descending provision functions as hospitality that calls for return.** Lexically, `ن ز ل:B005` is "guest-provision," `ر ز ق:B003` is "rain as provision," and `ن و ب:B001` is habitual return. Structurally, visible signs and food descend together, after the failed divine call in 40:12 and before the renewed command to call in 40:14. Provision's role is an enacted invitation: the giver supplies what a received guest needs, while `ينيب` names the answering return. The packet gives display, descent, provision, remembrance, and return; I infer the host-guest arrow connecting gift to acknowledgment. The ayah thus reads as material summons rather than as a sign list plus an unrelated condition.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:61, 40:64, and 40:79-81 expand the guest-provision image into a sustained habitat of time, shelter, food, transport, and recognizable benefit.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği görsel ya da içsel algıdır; belirli söz öbekleri ve bakma çabası ayrı kullanımlar olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın görme çekirdeği ile doğrudan göz tanıklığını ve görmeye çalışma bildiren bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi gözle ya da göz işlevi gören içsel kavrayışla algılamaktır. Gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan görme, bu anlamın duyusal ve tanıklığa dayalı gerçekleşimidir.

facets.statement: Görülebilir bir şeyi gözle veya benzer bir içsel kavrayışla algılama.
Bir şeyi gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan ve tanık olarak görme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, gözle görmeyi temel alır ve bazı anlatımlarda bu algıyı içsel kavrayışa kadar genişletir; doğrudan göz tanıklığı özellikle belirtilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ortak ekseni, bir konu hakkında zihinsel bir yargı veya görüş oluşturmaktır. Bilme ya da sanma değeri belirli tümce yapılarında, danışma ise başka birinin görüşünü istemede ortaya çıkar; bunlar yalın çekirdeğin eş düzeyli anlamları sayılmamalıdır.

facets.statement: Bir konu hakkında zihinde görüş, kanı veya yargı oluşturma.
